# Universal and negative collection matching in Criteria

Complete collection quantifiers in Immutables Criteria by adding `all()` and `none()` beside the existing `any()` matcher. They are available wherever Criteria exposes an iterable element matcher and return the same element matcher type as `any()`. Within that returned element matcher, scalar comparisons, nested object fields, and `with`, `not`, `and`, and `or` composition remain usable. The quantified surface also includes string prefix, containment, suffix, and length checks; optional presence and absence checks; and collection empty, non-empty, size, and containment checks.

For a collection or array and an element predicate, `any()` matches when at least one element satisfies the predicate, `all()` matches when every element satisfies it, and `none()` matches when no element satisfies it. An empty collection or array therefore matches `all()` and `none()`, but not `any()`. Object arrays and primitive arrays follow the same rules as iterable values.

A predicate belongs to one element at the quantifier where it is written, so values from different elements cannot be combined to satisfy a compound predicate. An element satisfies its predicate only when evaluation produces true. An equality predicate written on the element itself compares the entire element value; an element with additional or missing fields is not equal. A null element, or a missing or null value reached within an element, is not a match, including for a negative predicate; it therefore fails `all()` for that element but does not defeat `none()` when no element produces true. Within a compound predicate, a true `or` branch or false `and` branch is decisive even if another branch reaches a missing or null value, regardless of branch order.

Quantifiers may be nested and mixed when a nested quantifier is reached through an object field of the outer element, and each quantifier keeps its own element scope. A collection or array whose element is itself a collection or array is outside the required surface. Inherited collection predicates such as `isEmpty()`, `notEmpty()`, `hasSize()`, and `contains()` treat arrays and iterable values alike. Empty inner collections follow the same truth rules.

The matcher API and these semantics must work in the in-memory Criteria backend and in MongoDB query translation. Rendering a filter is not sufficient: the element operations named above must execute as real MongoDB find queries inside quantified scopes. String length counts every character, including line breaks. Nested quantifiers reached through object fields keep one scope per quantifier. A null or missing runtime collection matches none of the three quantifiers; it is not treated as empty. In MongoDB, a non-array stored value is also non-matching for new `all()` and `none()` scopes, and for `any()` inside a new quantifier scope. MongoDB queries must preserve same-element correlation for scalar and object arrays, compound predicates, and mixed nested quantifiers. Legacy flat positive `any()` queries must continue to match an equal scalar stored field value, and negative predicates on ordinary fields outside quantifier scopes keep their existing missing and null behavior.
I’ll trace the existing `any()` API, evaluator, and Mongo translation, then extend them with focused tests.
